source: SPHEREx L2 FLAGS header MSKN/MSKM/MSKD (checked 14 Nov 2026 on 2026W33_2A_0594_4D3, R7); hard list = IRSA mosaic reject list (Explanatory Supplement v2.1 §3.4.3). OVERFLOW, SOURCE, OUTLIER pass the mosaic tool.
saturation_note: OVERFLOW+BLOOM mean 'bright star': processing may mask them in the image but must raise the saturated warning/overlay rather than silently drop the target. For saturated targets (Barnard, RW Aur) BLOOM/TRANSIENT are set on the core in every frame, so a pure hard mask would blank the target; see per_target_notes.

0.name: TRANSIENT
0.plain: Something flashed here during the exposure (cosmic ray or a bright transient), so this pixel can't be trusted.

1.name: OVERFLOW
1.plain: Too bright: the detector saturated here, so the real brightness is higher than shown.

2.name: SUR_ERROR
2.plain: The on-board computer made an error while reading this pixel.

7.name: DICHROIC
7.plain: Edge of the detector where the beam splitter blocks most of the light.

9.name: MISSING_DATA
9.plain: Data for this pixel was lost on its way down from the satellite.

10.name: HOT
10.plain: Hot pixel: reads brighter than it should.

11.name: COLD
11.plain: Cold pixel: reads fainter than it should.

12.name: FULLSAMPLE
12.plain: Detailed read-out history exists for this pixel (technical note, nothing wrong).

14.name: PHANMISS
14.plain: A small detector-glow correction could not be applied here.

15.name: NONLINEAR
15.plain: Bright enough that the brightness correction is unreliable.

17.name: PERSIST
17.plain: Afterimage: left-over charge from an earlier bright source.

19.name: OUTLIER
19.plain: This pixel looks odd compared with its neighbours; kept, but treat with care.

20.name: CROSSTALK
20.plain: Faint copy of a bright object leaking in from elsewhere on the detector.

21.name: SOURCE
21.plain: A known star or galaxy sits on this pixel. Not a defect: this is the thing we want to see.

22.name: GHOST
22.plain: Faint reflection of a bright source in the same image.

23.name: GHOST_FPA
23.plain: Faint reflection of a bright source seen by another detector.

24.name: GHOST_EXT
24.plain: Faint reflection of a bright source just outside the field of view.

25.name: STREAK
25.plain: A line across the image, e.g. a satellite or asteroid trail.

26.name: BLOOM
26.plain: Light bleeding out of a very bright star along the detector.

27.name: SNOWBALL
27.plain: Round blob left by a cosmic-ray hit.

per_target_notes.barnards-star: OVERFLOW/BLOOM/TRANSIENT on the core in all 168 D1-D3 frames; core is NaN. Use D5/D6 or difference mode; position still measurable from the wings.
per_target_notes.rw-aurigae: OVERFLOW in 100/101 frames: bright (about Jy level). Flux values are lower limits.
per_target_notes.epsilon-indi-b: Faint (Gaia G=18) next to the bright star eps Indi A (~4.7 mag): watch GHOST/CROSSTALK/BLOOM near the target; check in QA.
per_target_notes.wise-0855: Faint, no saturation expected. Only visible above ~3.8 um (D5/D6); SOURCE may mark the AllWISE position, not today's.
per_target_notes.r-draconis: Mira at maximum can be bright in D1-D3; check OVERFLOW per epoch since flux changes by orders of magnitude over a cycle.
